title: Completed local tensor square of an adically formally smooth complete local algebra
statement:
Let $A\to R$ be a local homomorphism of commutative complete Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_A,\mathfrak m_R$, residue fields $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $l=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and finite residue extension $l/k$. Suppose $R$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_R$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Form $P=R\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-module-base-change] and the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q=\ker(P\to l)$, where $r\otimes s\mapsto\bar r\bar s$. Put $E=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}P_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qP_{\mathfrak q})^n$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $E$ is a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field $l$. The canonical maps $j_1,j_2:R\to E$ are local, induce the identity on $l$, are faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and make $E$ formally smooth over $R$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology. Multiplication $P\to R$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$, extends to a continuous local homomorphism $\mu:E\to R$ with $\mu j_1=\mu j_2=\mathrm{id}_R$. Here continuity is for maximal-ideal-adic topologies and local means inverse image of the maximal ideal equals the maximal ideal. Finally, with $J=j_2(\mathfrak m_R)E$, the map induced by $j_1$,
$$R/\mathfrak m_AR\longrightarrow E/J,$$
is faithfully flat. More precisely, if $F=(R/\mathfrak m_AR)\otimes_k l$ and $\mathfrak r=\ker(F\to l)$ for $\bar r\otimes a\mapsto\overline r a$, then $E/J$ is canonically isomorphic, compatibly with this map, to the maximal-ideal-adic completion of $F_{\mathfrak r}$.

source.place: EGA 0_I 7.7.1--7.7.7 (completed tensor products and their universal property); EGA 0_IV 19.3.5(iii)--(v), 19.3.6 (base change, localization and completion of formal smoothness). Local diagonal factor and closed-fibre comparison formulated by Q102; no single Stacks tag states this combined completed-local-tensor lemma. Read online English EGA; local EGA I and IV PDFs WANTED.

proof.text: Write $S=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS$. The ideal $H=(\mathfrak m_R\otimes1,1\otimes\mathfrak m_R)P$ is finitely generated: take generators of $\mathfrak m_R$ in each factor. Applying tensor-quotient base change to each factor gives $P/H\cong l\otimes_k l$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ is a $k$-basis of $l$, then $1\otimes b_1,\ldots,1\otimes b_d$ span this ring over its first $l$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so the finite-algebra Noetherian lemma makes $P/H$ Noetherian. Since $H\subset\mathfrak q$, choose finite ideal generators of $\mathfrak q/H$ and lift them to $\mathfrak q$. Together with the generators of $H$ they generate $\mathfrak q$: subtract the appropriate lifted combination from any element of $\mathfrak q$ to obtain an element of $H$. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated. By the fraction description of localization, $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ and $S/\mathfrak n=l$.

source.place: Tags 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00CO (definition-localization), 07BH (local rings); explicit finite-generator argument for the diagonal ideal.

proof.text: Apply the completion theorem for a finitely generated ideal with Noetherian quotient to $(S,\mathfrak n)$: its hypotheses hold because $S/\mathfrak n=l$ is a field. It gives that $E$ is Noetherian and complete for $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nE$. The completion-mod-power lemma gives, for every $N\ge1$, the canonical compatible surjections $\pi_N:E\to S/\mathfrak n^N$ with kernel $\mathfrak m^N$. In particular $E/\mathfrak m=l$. This application does not assume that $S$ is Noetherian.

The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal of $E$. Indeed, an element $x\notin\mathfrak m$ has nonzero residue in $l$; each $x_N=\pi_N(x)$ is a unit in the local ring $S/\mathfrak n^N$. Explicitly a representative of $x_N$ in $S$ lies outside $\mathfrak n$ and hence has an inverse in $S$. The inverses $x_N^{-1}$ are compatible, since a homomorphism takes an inverse to an inverse. They form an inverse for $x$ in $E$. Conversely no element of $\mathfrak m$ is a unit, since its residue is zero. Thus $E$ is complete Noetherian local with residue $l$. Under this residue identification, each composite $R\to P\to S\to E\to l$ is the residue map of $R$; consequently $j_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m_R$ and $j_i(\mathfrak m_R^N)\subset\mathfrak m^N$, proving locality, continuity and the identity residue maps.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 07BH (local rings) and 00M9 (section-completion); units and residue maps computed in compatible sequences.

proof.text: For the first $R$-algebra structure on $P$, adic formal smoothness is preserved by base change from $A\to R$ in the second factor. It holds for the ideal $I=(1\otimes\mathfrak m_R)P$. To verify it on $S$ for $\mathfrak n$, take a square-zero ideal $L\subset D$, an $R$-algebra map $g:S\to D/L$, and $N\ge1$ with $g(\mathfrak n^N)=0$. The restriction to $P$ kills $I^N$, so base-change formal smoothness gives an $R$-algebra lift $f:P\to D$. For $t\in P\setminus\mathfrak q$, $f(t)$ is invertible modulo $L$. Choose $b$ lifting its inverse, so $f(t)b=1+u$ with $u\in L$; then $b(1-u)$ is an inverse since $u^2=0$. Hence the formula $p/t\mapsto f(p)f(t)^{-1}$ defines a lift $S\to D$, reducing to $g$. It kills $\mathfrak n^{2N}$ because the image of $\mathfrak n^N$ lies in $L$. This verifies exactly the defining adic lifting property. Interchanging the two factors repeats the argument with $I=(\mathfrak m_R\otimes1)P$ and proves it for the second $R$-structure as well.

source.place: Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs), Definition 07EB/07NI (formal smoothness); localization lift written using fractions and square-zero inverses.

proof.text: Since $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated, preservation of adic formal smoothness by completion applies to each of the two maps $R\to S$. It makes $E$ formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak nE=\mathfrak m$-adic topology. Both $R$ and $E$ are Noetherian local rings and both $j_i$ are local, as already proved, so the adic-formally-smooth local flatness lemma shows that each $j_i$ is flat. The flat-local-homomorphism lemma then makes each $j_i$ faithfully flat.

The tensor-pushout property gives multiplication $P\to R$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$. For $t\notin\mathfrak q$ its product has nonzero residue in $l$, hence is a unit of $R$. Multiplication therefore defines $h:S\to R$ by the fraction formula. It sends $\mathfrak n$ into $\mathfrak m_R$, giving compatible ring maps $S/\mathfrak n^N\to R/\mathfrak m_R^N$. For $x=(x_N)_N\in E$ their values form a compatible sequence in $\varprojlim_N R/\mathfrak m_R^N$. Completeness of $R$ identifies that sequence with a unique element $\mu(x)\in R$. Coordinatewise operations prove that $\mu$ is a ring map, and $\ker\pi_N=\mathfrak m^N$ shows $\mu(\mathfrak m^N)\subset\mathfrak m_R^N$, so it is continuous. Its residue map is the identity of $l$, hence $\mu^{-1}(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m$. On either copy of $R$ its $N$th coordinate is the original element modulo $\mathfrak m_R^N$; separation of $R$ therefore gives $\mu j_1=\mu j_2=\mathrm{id}_R$.

source.place: Tags 0317 (definition-complete), 00CO (definition-localization), 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); tensor universal property used in More on Algebra Tag 07EG.

proof.text: Put $B=R/\mathfrak m_AR$ and $K=(1\otimes\mathfrak m_R)S$. Tensor-quotient base change identifies $P/(1\otimes\mathfrak m_R)P=R\otimes_A l$. This is $F=B\otimes_k l$: the forward map is $r\otimes a\mapsto[r]\otimes a$, and the inverse is $[r]\otimes a\mapsto r\otimes a$; the latter is independent of the lift because $\mathfrak m_A$ annihilates $l$. Both maps respect the balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors. The map $P\to l$ becomes $F\to l$, $[r]\otimes a\mapsto\bar r a$, so $\mathfrak q$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak r$. The map $S\to F_{\mathfrak r}$ sends $p/t$ to $\bar p/\bar t$ and kills $K$. Conversely $\bar p/\bar t\mapsto(p/t)\bmod K$ defines its inverse from $F_{\mathfrak r}$ to $S/K$: a lift $t$ of $\bar t\notin\mathfrak r$ lies outside $\mathfrak q$, and changing either lift by the quotient ideal changes the fraction by $K$. Thus $S/K\cong F_{\mathfrak r}$, taking $(\mathfrak n+K)/K$ to its maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact) and Tag 00CO (definition-localization); explicit tensor and fraction identifications.

proof.text: For $N\ge1$ write $K_N=(K+\mathfrak n^N)/\mathfrak n^N$. There are compatible short exact sequences of $S$-modules $0\to K_N\to S/\mathfrak n^N\to S/(K+\mathfrak n^N)\to0$. The maps $K_{N+1}\to K_N$ are surjective: represent an element by $k\in K$ and use that same $k$ at level $N+1$. Inverse-limit exactness for towers with surjective kernel transitions therefore gives a surjective ring map $\theta:E\to\varprojlim_N S/(K+\mathfrak n^N)$. By the quotient identification in the previous step, the target is precisely the maximal-ideal-adic completion of $F_{\mathfrak r}$.

source.place: Tag 03CA (lemma-Mittag-Leffler), applied to quotient towers indexed by the positive integers; Tag 00M9 (section-completion).

proof.text: The ideal $J$ of the statement is $KE$. Under $E/\mathfrak m^N\cong S/\mathfrak n^N$, its image is exactly $K_N$: a sum of products of generators from $K$ and coefficients of $E$ reduces to one from $S$ because $E\to S/\mathfrak n^N$ is surjective; conversely every $k\in K$ is an image from $J$. Hence $\ker\theta=\bigcap_{N\ge1}(J+\mathfrak m^N)$. Apply Krull intersection to the Noetherian ring $E$, the ideal $\mathfrak m$ contained in its Jacobson radical, and the cyclic $E$-module $E/J$. It gives $\bigcap_N\mathfrak m^N(E/J)=0$, so $\ker\theta=J$. The resulting ring isomorphism $E/J\cong\widehat{F_{\mathfrak r}}$ sends the class of $j_1(r)$ at level $N$ to the class of $[r]\otimes1$ modulo the $N$th power of the maximal ideal. It is therefore canonical and compatible with the map from $B$ claimed in the statement.

source.place: Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2), applied to E/J.

proof.text: The quotient $B$ of $R$ is Noetherian by the surjective-image lemma; it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_AR$ (units lift from the local ring $R$) and residue $l$. The basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $l/k$ makes $1\otimes b_1,\ldots,1\otimes b_d$ a finite spanning set for $F=B\otimes_k l$ over $B$. Thus $F$ is Noetherian by the finite-algebra lemma and $F_{\mathfrak r}$ is Noetherian by the localization lemma. Moreover the composite $B\to F\to l$ is the residue map of $B$, so the inverse image of $\mathfrak r$ in $B$ is exactly $\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); the finite spanning set and the contracted prime are computed explicitly.

proof.text: The field-extension-base-change lemma makes $B\to F=B\otimes_k l$ faithfully flat, in particular flat. Localizing at $\mathfrak r$, whose contraction is $\mathfrak m_B$, gives a flat local map $B=B_{\mathfrak m_B}\to F_{\mathfrak r}$. Since $F_{\mathfrak r}$ is Noetherian local, its completion map is faithfully flat, in particular flat. Composition of flat ring maps therefore makes $B\to\widehat{F_{\mathfrak r}}$ flat. This composite is local: its residue map is $B\to l$ by the explicit finite-quotient maps above. Equivalently, via $\theta$, the target is $E/J$, which is local because $J\subset\mathfrak m$, and its maximal ideal contracts to $\mathfrak m_B$. The flat-local-homomorphism lemma proves faithful flatness. The compatible isomorphism of step 9 identifies this map with the map $R/\mathfrak m_AR\to E/J$ induced by $j_1$, completing all clauses.

tool_uses.why: Step 2 uses its general finitely-generated-ideal/Noetherian-quotient completion criterion; the tensor square before completion need not be Noetherian and the unit has no replacement criterion.
Step 4 uses the general adic formal-smoothness base-change theorem on the two tensor factors; this is a commutative-algebra tool, not a replacement for the six-functor route.
Step 5 uses preservation of adic formal smoothness under completion of a finitely generated ideal, a generic ring theorem not furnished by this unit.
Step 5 uses flatness of an adically formally smooth local map of Noetherian local rings; the unit has no ring-theoretic replacement.
Step 8 uses exactness of an inverse limit of short exact module towers when the kernel transition maps are surjective; this generic algebra tool is needed for the closed-fibre quotient.
